name: Elmer Spencer Kulp
notable_stories: Filed for a birth certificate later in life with confirmation from his uncle Tate McPhail
Elmer and Amy waited nine years to have children because times were hard in the Depression and they were helping other family members.
Elmer was not interested in family history, so he did not receive one of Dradie's family books.
milestones: Married Amy Ritchey (m. 4 Jun 1931, Bellingham, Whatcom Co, Washington)
education: Elmer Kulp went to school in Albion, Washington, where Alice Hittle was a schoolmate, and later attended Albion school reunions.
Elmer attended school in Schragg, then graduated from Albion High School.
career: Elmer and Amy farmed in Whatcom County from 1931 to 1954.
sources: Family research emails, 2011–2013 (John and Barbara Adams with Irma Kulp Zacher, George F. Adams, Bill Allen and others)
notes: Spouse corrected to ritchey_amy (was erroneously self-referencing).
CORRECTION 2026-09-22: Mother set to mcphail_mary_emily, the only recorded wife of John Jacob Kulp (m. 15 Aug 1897; she d. 1931); confirmed by Brendan Adams.
Elmer, Amy, and the Burk and Simons households belonged to the Delta Grange (a farmers' association, not a church). [Family research emails, email 48]
Open question: The Kulp lineage numbering in email 23 skips 8 and uses 9 twice (John Jacob Kulp and Elmer Spencer Kulp). The generation numbers are not reliable. [Family research emails, email 23]
